metrics.boundary: One distinct provider+model judgment per frozen prompt, not a human verdict. Shared responses are paired observations, not independent samples. Abstentions are scored separately from answer correctness. No acceptance threshold is inferred from these medians.

bootstrap.unit: original synthetic family; not case, condition, shared prompt or model call
bootstrap.metric: Confirmed-correct answers / planned questions; failed judgment remains unknown, not classified incorrect. Pair differences use only questions graded in both conditions.
bootstrap.limitation: Post hoc descriptive intervals for 12 fixed synthetic families. Shared prompts and one judge draw do not become independent replications. Not a population, repeated-model, human or product quality acceptance claim.

interpretation: Only historical reader inputs v2 and their unchanged completed reader responses are graded. This is not a run of the latest production code or corrected routing inputs v3.
Different reader and judge models satisfy the recorded model-review boundary; the 407 valid calls are not independent human judgments.
719 paired observations share 407 valid prompt judgments. All 408 distinct judge inputs were dispatched, but one provider failure leaves executionComplete=false.
High conditional answer-correctness medians do not compensate for low answering coverage. Genuine refusals have null correctness and are not counted as correct.
Time and knowledge ablations repeat all 120 original prompts: zero differences cannot estimate their feature benefit. A later single-family knowledge control is not this experiment.
Hypothesis simulation is unsupported by the Phase 2 contract; its refusal counts are scope protection, not a request to implement later-phase simulation.
No v1 ratings are combined, no failed prompt is retried, no answer, gold or model judgment is rewritten. The one known failure remains a separate unknown denominator.
